body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_1,M_1]}\{(T-\kappa_T(C))^{-1}\sum_{t=\kappa_T(C)+1}^{T}Y_t\prod_{j=t-\kappa_T(C)}^{t}e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\},\quad R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)},\quad q_C=(C-1)/C\), uniformly for \(C\ge1\).

sampling_model.design: One behavior-stationary trajectory from a time-homogeneous finite POMDP; randomness comes from the joint reward-transition kernel and the known behavior randomization.
sampling_model.units: The observations are \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\), with real rewards satisfying fixed conditional first- and second-moment envelopes \(M_1,M_2\); \(H_t,d_b,d_e\) remain unobserved.
sampling_model.treatment: The revealed action alphabet is any finite nonempty set and both policies are known and memoryless in \(X_t\); the matching lower bound already holds on a binary-action subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: One-step action ratios are bounded by \(e^{\zeta}\), and the unobserved joint stationary ratio is bounded by \(C\); the induced distance radius is \(q_C=(C-1)/C\), while neither stationary law nor its ratio is supplied.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No latent alphabet, transition kernel, reward regression, stationary law, proxy, emission rank, or finite-memory bound is known or estimated as a class-membership condition; the attaining estimator uses only observed rewards and revealed policy ratios.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 give the PHIW upper rate on a finite-action conditional first- and second-moment class, while Theorem 6 gives the unrestricted POMDP exponent and Section 3.2 leaves distributionally overlapping hidden-state hard instances open.

Strong or square-integrable stationary density-ratio control supports root-\(T\) behavior for truncated doubly robust evaluation in fully observed MDPs, while heavier ratio tails produce slower regimes.
Latent-state density-ratio coverage is weaker than belief coverage, and future-dependent value guarantees can retain exponentially large outcome or belief quantities without the stronger conditions.
Generic partially observable off-policy evaluation can have arbitrarily large bias, while recovery in the decoupled POMDP uses invertibility and conditional-independence structure.
Double reinforcement learning attains the semiparametric efficiency bound in observed Markov models using estimated \(q\)-functions and marginalized density ratios.
Long-run average policy outcomes admit estimation and confidence intervals in a fully observed Markov mobile-health model.

body.tldr: Uniformly over every \(C\ge1\), let \(q_C=(C-1)/C\).  On Hu and Wager's finite-action conditional first- and second-moment POMDP class intersected with \(d_e\le Cd_b\), the exact cardinality-uniform minimax MSE is \(T^{-1}+T^{-2/(2+t_0\zeta)}q_C^{2\{1-2/(2+t_0\zeta)\}}\), with constants independent of \(C\) and no logarithmic factor.  The exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C_T-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near equality.  Radius-adaptive observable partial-history weighting attains the law, while a signed-depth binary bounded-reward subclass supplies the all-estimator converse and the equality endpoint supplies the parametric floor.

project_justification.gap: HuWager2023 proves PHIW upper bounds under conditional reward moments and the unrestricted POMDP minimax exponent, but its Section 3.2 leaves overlapping hidden-state hard instances open and provides no stationary-overlap-radius phase diagram.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a uniform-in-\(C\) observed-law testing modulus that joins exact stationary equality, shrinking latent stationary overlap, and every fixed overlap radius without observing the latent density ratio.
project_justification.fill: The signed-depth reset family keeps \(d_e/d_b\) within the prescribed radius and yields observed-path divergence \(T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\), while the retained PHIW bias factor \(q_C\alpha^k\) produces a radius-adaptive history choice.  Together with the parametric pair, these calculations prove the complete uniform frontier.

body.related_work: HuWager2023 is the theorem anchor: its Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 analyze PHIW for general finite actions under conditional first- and second-moment bounds, its Theorem 6 proves the unrestricted POMDP exponent, and Section 3.2 asks whether the lower bound persists under distributional overlap.  The present uniform theorem intersects that published moment class with \(d_e\le Cd_b\) and answers the question for every radius at once.  Its converse is proved on a normalized, scaled Rademacher signed-depth family with binary actions and bounded rewards; that hard family is a subclass of the published moment model, so its lower bound transfers to the larger class, while the upper calculation extends over all finite actions.  MehrabiWager2025 treats observable stationary ratios in fully observed MDPs and therefore does not supply the latent-radius modulus.  ZhangJiang2024, TennenholtzShalitMannor2020, KallusUehara2020, and LiaoKlasnjaMurphy2021 mark respectively the belief-coverage, invertibility, observed-MDP efficiency, and fully observed long-run inference boundaries.  LuckettEtAl2020 and MaahsEtAl2012 motivate HuWager2023 Section 5.2; the accompanying proposition concerns only an explicitly refreshed finite discretization, not the original continuous simulator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The observed-filtration posterior bound, the full stationary-initial-window KL calculation, the radius frontier, and the finite insulin-grid certificate are proved.  Remaining limitations are substantive rather than proof gaps: latent stationary overlap is imposed rather than testable from the observed trajectory, the theorem is finite-state and cardinality-uniform but does not cover the original continuous glucose simulator, and it gives mean-squared-error rates rather than confidence intervals or policy-learning regret.
body.honest_scope: The result is uniform over \(C\ge1\), all finite observed, latent, and action cardinalities, and all revealed policy pairs in the conditional-moment class; comparison constants may depend on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) but not on \(C,T\), or cardinality.  The hard family uses binary actions, bounded scaled Rademacher rewards, and \(2(Q+1)\) latent states, so it transfers upward to the finite-action moment class but does not prove a converse under a uniformly bounded hidden alphabet.  At \(C=1\) the stationary laws coincide and immediate weighting is parametric; for fixed \(C>1\) the slower exponent remains.  The finite refreshed insulin model demonstrates the implication without asserting that the original continuous simulator satisfies finite-state contraction or latent stationary overlap.
body.interpretation: Bounded latent occupancy helps continuously but does not by itself restore parametric precision at a fixed nonunit radius.  The hidden-state term is negligible only when \(Tq_C^2=O(1)\); beyond that elbow, the optimal observable history grows as \(\log(Tq_C^2)\).  Thus a quantitative physiological-occupancy assurance can justify shorter histories, but fixed \(C>1\) still leaves the Hu--Wager partial-observability exponent and does not replace collection of informative state or proxy measurements.
